versions.text: Criterion: Verify that the worst case engine stall loads are within Interface Control Document (ICD) limits. Standard: To ensure structural integrity of the air inlet system, worst case engine stall loads (e.g., hammer shock) are within required limits. Note: The inlet structure design is governed by section 5 requirements. Method of Compliance: Verification methods include analysis, test, inspection and review of documentation. Engine air inlet components requirements are verified by inspection of design documents. Maximum induced inlet stall pressures generated by inlet/engine anomalies are validated by inspection of analyses and/or test. Capability of the components to withstand required inlet stall pressure is verified through component proof analysis and test.

Standard: Worst-case engine stall loads (e.g., hammer shock) are within air inlet system limits as documented in the engine-to-air-vehicle ICD. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Examination of the ICD verifies that engine air inlet component structural overpressure limits or requirements are defined. Analysis.
  (1) Analysis is conducted to define maximum surge pressure. Loads are verified to be within ICD limits. Test.
    (1) Lab test: Engine test in a ground-based sea level test cell is conducted to calibrate surge overpressure predictions.
